content:
ops-bot: alert: sudden apiserver 5xx/connection-reset spike in eu-west1 observed by LB healthchecks :rotating_light:
harper: noticed controller-manager lost leader lease repeatedly for ~7m, controllers stuck in crashloopbackoff
diego: apiserver logs show lots of "connection reset by peer" and long TLS handshake times around the same window
zoe: DNS metrics for the region show a small surge in NXDOMAIN + SERVFAIL from our cluster DNS cache layer at the same time :thinking_face:
ravi: NVMe pool iops look normal, but NAT gateway conntrack entries are at ~88% and ephemeral ports trending up rapidly
marie: GPU attach subsystem spiked with parallel attach attempts after a large batch job scheduled -> many kubelet diffs and watch callbacks to apiserver
tim: that combination (attach retries + DNS blips + conntrack pressure) could cause proxy resets and controller lease eviction
harper: can someone run a quick grep for "failed to acquire lease" in controller-manager logs?
diego: running: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/controller-manager --since=20m | grep "failed to acquire lease" || true
diego: output: ~220 matches clustered ~2025-12-03T04:12-04:18, aligns with LB spikes
zoe: dnsmasq cache hit-rate dropped to 60% during the spike, upstream queries spiked -> more connection churn to external resolvers
ravi: conntrack increase caused many short-lived 4-tuple sockets to pile up in TIME_WAIT, exhausting ports for new TLS handshakes
marie: quick mitigation ideas: 1) enable HTTP keepalive reuse on apiserver LB so fewer new TCP handshakes 2) throttle GPU attach fanout 3) extend leader-election lease duration slightly while stabilizing
tim: added an iptables rule to preferentially accept established connections and rate-limit SYNs from the provisioner pool; applied on eu-west1 NATs
harper: pushed a config canary to provisioner to introduce randomized exponential backoff for attach attempts (base 2s -> max 120s)
diego: temporarily reduced the apiserver non-critical max-requests-inflight to 300 to keep controlplane responsive to leader heartbeats
zoe: also warmed dnsmasq cache by pre-seeding common upstreams and pointed cluster resolvers to a local upstream cache pod to cut external query burst
ravi: applied small conntrack.max bump from 65k -> 150k as short term headroom, monitoring for side effects
marie: post-mitigation, controller-manager lease failures dropped to single digits in 10m window; apiserver 5xx rate down to baseline
harper: great. next steps: 1) keep provisioner backoff in prod for 1h, 2) deploy LB keepalive tuning across eu-west1 frontends, 3) investigate eBPF socket coalescing to reduce syscalls on high churn flows
tim: eBPF coalesce prototype sounds promising — can reduce SYN storms and consolidate retransmits. I'll spike a PoC on staging
diego: longer term: consider pinned small reserved GPU capacity for scheduled large batch jobs to avoid sudden attach floods, and DNS cache HA for the region
zoe: also add a health-check that tracks DNS cache hit-rate and raises before apiserver errors surface
marie: finance note: keeping conntrack elevated long-term increases NAT gateway memory; estimate extra cost ~ $300/mo per gateway for larger instances if we go that route
harper: I'm updating incident notes and runbook: incident-ref: apiserver-dns-connship-2025-12-03, adding rollback steps for each mitigation
ops-bot: incident log appended: runbook-ref: controlplane-tcp-reuse-v1
diego: marking thread as in-progress, will post metrics in 10m :white_check_mark:
